question: Could MMU page protection enforce the checked guest permissions for almost every access, with exact 4 KiB checks only where a 16 KiB host page has mixed 4 KiB permissions?

census.method: Opt-in diagnostic in the trusted require() path (docs/experiments/guest-page-census-diagnostic.patch, not shipped). Counts every checked guest access; flags accesses to 16 KiB host pages whose four 4 KiB permissions differ, and writes to host pages containing published code.
census.route: iPad Air 11-inch (M4) Simulator; launch, menus, offline Katabatic host with two bots, observer gameplay.

startup_and_loading.note: All counted within the first 134M accesses (startup).

fault_emulation_spike.source: tests/fault_emulation_spike.c (component test; not linked into TribesPad)
fault_emulation_spike.method: Guest view plus vm_remap RW alias. Uniform host pages get native protections; a mixed host page is PROT_NONE. SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler decodes the AArch64 scalar load/store (incl. LDP/STP), checks the exact 4 KiB table, aborts on violation or emulates through the alias and resumes.
fault_emulation_spike.macos: PASS: native 0.94 ns/rmw on uniform pages; emulated 2130 ns/access; 4 denied accesses (mixed read, mixed write, uniform read-only write, straddle) abort before effect; 4 threads.
fault_emulation_spike.ios_simulator: PASS (xcrun simctl spawn, iOS 26.5 Simulator): native 0.53 ns/rmw; emulated 2090 ns/access; same 4 aborts; 4 threads.
fault_emulation_spike.not_covered: SIMD, atomics (LDXR/STXR, LSE), pre/post-index forms, publication concurrency inside the handler, physical iOS devices, debugger interaction.

estimate: At ~84M checked accesses/s in gameplay, 0.47 per million is ~40 emulated faults/s (~0.1 ms/s). Removing the out-of-line software check from ~70% of game-thread self time is the only lever found large enough to approach playable frame rates; it is a structural change and still needs full design, tests and an offline-match measurement.
